scope: Independent review of the persisted developer-promotion confirmation slice, including authenticated loopback API, direct board-bound and disconnected Planner/Generator, Delivery continuation, SQLite reload, user-only clarification parsing, AgentsPlugin hard dependencies, Web dependency getters, and the actual Cordis root composition. This is external-agent evaluation, not live dsh Agent execution or full Issue 92 acceptance.

criteria.acceptance: Unapproved WorkItems and caller-supplied confirmation cannot start board-bound planning or implementation
criteria.evidence: E2 passes fresh unapproved WorkItems, caller confirmed:true, forged sourceApproval, missing WorkItem, wrong-project scope, and both direct roles across manual/external-agent/huntianling-runtime executor tags. Disconnected Planner and Generator reject supplied WorkItem ids with no runs or candidate artifacts. E2 and E4 exercise the real Cordis HTTP composition: unapproved planning is denied and approved runs belong to the registered agents service. The original F1 probe now passes: rejected -> ordinary approved leaves Planner HTTP 400, Generator denied, Delivery denied and fresh SQLite-backed resolution denied, with approval null. Explicit authenticated renewal restores planning.

criteria.acceptance: Approved inputs preserve source quotes, goals, actors, and acceptance across reload
criteria.evidence: E2 includes independent HTTP-only session creation, customer message submission, analysis, candidate update, authenticated developer promotion, and planning. Forged actorId is ignored; the stored actor is reviewer. Caller goal/quotes/acceptance replacements do not replace approved inputs. A fresh Board over the same temporary SQLite store returns deeply equal confirmed inputs. Existing tests additionally preserve document chunk and full-text quotes through reload.

criteria.acceptance: Changed source, candidate, or WorkItem scope invalidates approval and blocks continuation
criteria.evidence: E2 independently changes WorkItem title, body, sourceInput, and acceptance; both Planner and Generator reject each drift, fresh SQLite-backed Board resolution rejects it, and mismatched candidate reapproval fails. Candidate actor changes require explicit renewal. User-source changes block the next delivery step and interrupted Agent resume; replacing the approval cannot resume old Planner/Generator runs or an old delivery checkpoint after recreating Board, Runtime, and Delivery. Unchanged checkpoint recovery succeeds. Existing tests also cover attachment drift. Assistant/system parser inputs cannot alter draft fields or answer questions after the latest clarify.ts repair; these are parser defense tests, not a demonstrated current API injection.

criteria.acceptance: The explicit approval action can renew matching scope; generic status edits cannot issue approval
criteria.evidence: E2 verifies explicit renewal and rejects ordinary candidate status:approved. Session rejection now clears approvals in the same snapshot update; an ordinary status change cannot restore them. The original independent authenticated F1 probe passes, including both runtime/Delivery denial and SQLite reload, followed by successful explicit renewal bound to reviewer rather than a forged actor. A separate independent legacy fixture writes a rejected session retaining an old approval into temporary SQLite, reloads it, then tries ordinary approved and ready_for_analysis updates: both clear the old approval and remain denied after another reload. The repository regression also verifies another session's approved inputs remain unchanged.

criteria.acceptance: Delivery and HTTP planning use the same confirmation checks without fabricating inputs
criteria.evidence: E2 and E4 verify authenticated HTTP planning and Delivery against both service factories and the actual Cordis root composition. Unapproved /plan returns 400; approved /plan preserves original inputs and its run id is found in ctx.get('huntianling.agents'). Approved HTTP Delivery returns 201 and is blocked by the missing prepared environment, not a missing service. Direct-runtime probes verify approved source fields replace caller-provided fields; continuation and reload recheck approval. Source inspection confirms both paths use resolveConfirmedRequirement. Executed late-service tests verify agents/delivery/harness getters register and withdraw after Web starts, without stale-service side effects or implicit runtime fallback when the explicit agents getter returns undefined. This passes this slice's input-resolution criterion, not actual dsh execution or customer delivery.

resolvedFindings.title: Generic session status updates revive a rejected approval without explicit reapproval
beforeRepairReproduction: Create an isolated requirement and explicitly approve its candidate, retaining the persisted approval.
As an authenticated project developer, PATCH /api/v1/intake/sessions/:id with status:rejected; HTTP planning then returns 400.
PATCH the same session with status:approved using the ordinary update route; do not call /approve.
POST /api/v1/work-items/:id/plan returns 200. Direct manual Generator status is completed and Delivery.start status is running.
Recreate Board from the temporary SQLite store: the old approval is unchanged and resolveConfirmedRequirement succeeds.
resolvedFindings.expected: Rejected approval remains unusable until the explicit approval action issues a current approval. Ordinary status edits must not restore execution authorization.
resolvedFindings.beforeRepairCause: updateIntakeSession persisted status changes without invalidating candidate approvals; resolveConfirmedRequirement rejected only while the session was currently rejected. Returning to approved removed that check while every stored digest still matched.
resolvedFindings.repairVerification: E2 passes the original F1 probe, strengthened with explicit Generator, Delivery, reload, null-approval and authenticated-renewal assertions. It also passes an independent legacy rejected-SQLite probe and the repository's other-session isolation regression. updateIntakeSession now clears matching-session approvals when either old or new status is rejected, in the same snapshot update.

executionEvidence.observed: All source files matched the tested temporary build after the final run. The official customer-e2e script also matched by diff -q. Hashes below identify the evaluated snapshot, not future main-line changes.

The repository's actual Cordis root plugin and HTTP suite pass all 15 checks. Unapproved Story delivery is rejected with 409 and unapproved /plan with 400. Approved /plan carries persisted candidate/actor approval and its run id is present in the registered agents service. Delivery reaches its environment gate. The suite also verifies isolated roles, project access, intake/attachments, hierarchy, projections, evidence denial, logout, and native diagnostic-only CI using dependency-free temporary scripts and pnpm install --offline --ignore-scripts. No external account, provider, production repository or live dsh task is used.

compositionReevaluation.resolvedObservation: Before the Web getter repair, this evaluator reproduced customer-e2e 13/15 with both delivery checks failing, and an independent root-composition probe showed Delivery registered in ctx while HTTP returned 400 huntianling.delivery is required. Main reported discovering the production-composition chain independently. After its repair, E4 is 15/15 and all four independent composition/disconnected-runtime probes pass. The missing-service observation is resolved, not an open finding.
compositionReevaluation.sourceInspection: AgentsPlugin injects skills, board and environment as hard dependencies and requires all three before creating the runtime. Runtime's Planner/Generator guard also activates for any supplied workItemId even without Board. WebPlugin reads optional agents/delivery/harness via ctx.get getters; server.start overrides spread-created values with getters again. An explicitly supplied agents property resolving undefined is returned as undefined rather than selecting the fallback runtime. E2 now also executes all three late-service getter registration/withdrawal paths and the standalone absent-property fallback; this is not a complete Cordis hot-reload matrix.
compositionReevaluation.probeCorrection: The initial independent Delivery probe expected 200, but the source route returns 201 for creation. After missing-service repair it returned 201 with the correct environment blocker; the temporary probe was corrected to assert 201 and rerun. This assertion correction is not a product defect or weakened approval check.
